When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most", "witness": "COUNTEREXAMPLE to the claim (11) that among the 2^{n+1}-2 sums of nonempty proper subsets some two consecutive ones differ by at most d=1/(2^{n+1}-1). Take n=1, m=2, a_1=0.1, a_2=0.9. The nonempty proper subsets are {1},{2} with sums 0.1 and 0.9; the only consecutive gap is 0.8 > 1/3 = d. So no pair S,T of nonempty proper subsets satisfies (12), and the strategy built from it does not exist. The inference is also a NON-SEQUITUR in general: 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to less than 1 only yields a gap below 1/(2^{n+1}-3), which exceeds d. (The standard argument uses all 2^{n+1} subset sums including 0 and 1, giving 2^{n+1}-1 gaps summing to exactly 1; the text does not do this.)", "load_bearing": "In the case m=n+1 the entire Xiang Yu strategy (both the 'one of A,B empty' branch and the common-refinement branch) is constructed from the pair S,T satisfying (12), which is derived solely from (11)."}},
